newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Italy government gets go-ahead for mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Italy government gets go-ahead for mini-budget.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi got support from coalition partners on Wednesday for a corrective budget to put Italy back on track for European economic and monetary union (EMU), party leaders said.
The mini-budget is expected to include around 16 trillion lire ($9.5 billion) of deficit-cutting measures and will almost certainly be approved by the cabinet on Thursday.

"There was broad backing for the government on its global aims...although there is some fine tuning to be done," said Franco Marini, head of the Popular Party, following a meeting of coalition leaders and cabinet ministers.
Fausto Bertinotti, head of the hardleft Communist Refoundation, told reporters that he had won his battle to prevent any further tax hikes or cuts to social spending.
"The meeting went well," he said. "There will be no new taxes and no reduction in welfare spending."

Centre-right parties had called on Prodi to embark on an overhaul of the welfare state with the mini-budget, arguing that structural spending changes were the only way to ensure that Italy was ready for the launch of the single European currency.

A corrective budget was needed after data from the first quarter indicated that Italy's deficit this year was heading towards 3.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) against three percent demanded by the Maastricht Treaty.

Refoundation, which holds the balance of power in the lower house of parliament, had threatened to bring Prodi down if he touched social spending. Bertinotti indicated that with the budget out of the way, he was now willing to discuss reform.
